newsitem.title: UK: Refuge meets biggest shareholder on merger.
newsitem.headline: Refuge meets biggest shareholder on merger.

text.p: Senior executives from life assurers Refuge Group and United Friendly, who earlier this month announced plans to merge, met Refuge's biggest institutional shareholder on Friday, a day after another big Refuge shareholder said it would vote against the merger.

Britannic Assurance, which owns just over 10 percent of Refuge shares and a much smaller stake in United Friendly, said it expected to make up its mind about the proposals next week after meeting the two insurers earlier on Friday.
A special meeting for shareholders to vote on the merger has been scheduled for September 9.

Perpetual Plc, which owns just over seven percent of Refuge, said on Thursday it would vote against the merger saying it was not convinced Refuge directors had secured the best possible terms for shareholders.
It is not so much the logic of the deal, but the valuation of Refuge's assets that has upset some shareholders.

In particular, Perpetual believes that, during discussions with the UK government, Refuge could have unlocked more "orphan" assets for shareholders from its ordinary branch of business, not just 430 million stg identified in the industrial branch. A spokesman for Britannic described the issues as "complex."
Sources close to Refuge and United are confident the deal will go through, despite the opposition from some areas.
Former insurance analyst Alan Richards, who has already voiced doubts about the merger, plans next week to publish a document outlining how the terms could be changed.

SBC Warburg in a research note did not dispute the logic of the merger, but said, "failure to quantify costs and savings and the inability to repatriate excess capital to shareholders means that the benefits of the deal are not overwhelming."
The broker said disappointment with regard to Refuge's net asset value has been deflected into "largely unfounded" arguments that the terms of the merger favour United Friendly.
But it also noted that holders of United Friendly ordinary shares, which carry with them voting rights, have been treated disproportionately favourably.
